items.text: Premium package launches at ₹2,499 per month
Existing customers get a 15% upgrade discount within the first 30 days, not publicly advertised
A clearly defined list of premium benefits before sales actively promotes the package
Quarterly consultation sessions included in the premium package, optional, while customer numbers stay manageable
Initial marketing campaign budget is ₹3 lakh
Additional marketing spending requires approval based on campaign performance thresholds
Leads split into high, medium and low intent: direct calls, personalized emails, existing newsletter
No additional sales or support hiring before launch
Reassess staffing after the first four weeks
November 4 launch date remains the target
October 28 is the internal readiness decision point
If the critical feature is not stable by October 28 the launch moves to November 11
Prepare frequently asked questions and onboarding materials to reduce repetitive support requests
Launch not evaluated solely on revenue; retention matters more than maximizing initial sales

Success metrics: premium upgrades, lead conversion rate, trial-to-paid conversion, customer acquisition cost, 30-day churn, support request volume, response time, webinar registrations, marketing-qualified leads
Specific metric targets established before launch
A dashboard available during the first week
First 30 days are the primary evaluation period
Finalize the premium package feature list and coordinate the October 28 readiness review
Prepare the first-stage ₹3 lakh marketing campaign and define performance thresholds for additional spending
Segment the 120 existing leads and create the outreach strategy
Prepare the customer-success contingency plan and premium onboarding documentation
Identify potential temporary support resources without committing to additional hiring
Finalize the financial model and acceptable customer acquisition cost thresholds
Approve the final launch communication and review the October 28 readiness assessment
Confusion and mixed reactions around the ₹2,499 pricing
Reducing the price before launch makes it hard to raise later without customer dissatisfaction
Customers expect more benefits for paying about ₹1,000 more per month
Sales representatives might promise features the product team has not committed to
Customer success lacks capacity for personalized calls to every premium customer
A smaller campaign could limit awareness and make the launch look unsuccessful
Sales team may need temporary help if lead volume increases significantly
Two features still in testing; the critical one may not be stable by October 28, delaying launch
Delaying the launch would require changing external marketing commitments
Lowering the price could signal the product is worth less
A strong launch could flood customer success; beyond about 50 new premium accounts in the first month response times could rise substantially
Whether the existing customer-success team can handle demand if the launch significantly exceeds expectations
Enough evidence to proceed with the proposed price; evaluate conversion after launch
